chapter: Retirement and the future of big bands
title: Retirement lifestyle and refusing offers to tour
summary: He declines Willard Alexander's tour feelers and describes his new life between Palm Springs and San Diego.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Oh, beautiful publicity. But it was -- so many outrageous things happened, I mean that it's really more a life story, than shall we say that has to do with the music world, although it did happen on account of the music world. But I want to get back to one thing, and that was that I said that '73, that appearance up in Canada was the last thing I've done, and probably will be the last thing I've done

musically, because I've turned down, oh, feelers from -- Willard Alexander calls me every once in a while and says, "Hey, what about --," I know exactly what happened, he found one big money date and he wants to hinge a whole tour on one date, and then you've got to go through all that, the arrangements I have are getting old. I would have to get some new things, and I would have to buy a wardrobe. My whole lifestyle has changed, and I'm very happy with it. I'm into a different thing, fortunately, because I was able to do it gradually. I didn't just cut it off and say that's it, and I started changing over, and I am into a different lifestyle and I like it.
You spend, you said, seven months of the year, is that right, in Palm Springs, in the desert --
And five months here. And if we feel like taking a trip someplace we take it.

And it's -- I'm very happy with it, and I cannot under any circumstances ever imagine myself going back in the band business, although I do enjoy hearing a good band, and when they come around where they're near me and I can go hear them, I do.
So long as you don't have to come into Los Angeles, right?
Well, I don't have anything against Los Angeles, except that I have no base of operations there anymore.
